q-cf-fit.label: Choose between the confused words
q-cf-fit.summary: A sentence with a blank, and the pair it is usually confused with among the options.

q-cf-spot.label: The confused word inside a sentence
q-cf-spot.summary: One part of the sentence uses the partner word by mistake.

q-cf-replace.label: Replace the highlighted phrase, or say none is needed
q-cf-replace.summary: A sentence highlights a phrase built on a confused word; pick the correct replacement, or 'No substitution required' if it is already correct.

rules.text: Several pairs differ only as noun and verb: advice (noun) / advise (verb), practice (noun) / practise (verb), effect (noun) / affect (verb), licence (noun) / license (verb). Decide which part of speech the slot needs first.
rules.ok: Take my advice; I advise you to wait. The effect was clear; it did not affect me.
rules.bad: Take my advise; the affect was clear.

rules.text: Some pairs differ by one letter and have nothing else in common: principal (chief, or head of a college) / principle (a rule); stationary (not moving) / stationery (paper and pens); complement (completes) / compliment (praise); desert (sand) / dessert (sweet).

Some pairs are close in sense and so get swapped: eminent (famous) / imminent (about to happen); continual (repeated with breaks) / continuous (without a break); childish (silly) / childlike (innocent); economic (of the economy) / economical (thrifty); credible (believable) / credulous (too ready to believe).
rules.ok: An eminent judge warned of an imminent crisis.
rules.bad: An imminent judge warned of an eminent crisis.

rules.text: Lie, rise and sit take no object; lay, raise and set take one. Lie-lay-lain is to rest; lay-laid-laid is to put something down.
rules.ok: He lies down after lunch. He laid the book on the table.
rules.bad: He lays down after lunch. He lied the book on the table.

rules.text: First decide whether the highlighted phrase is already correct; if it is, the answer is 'No substitution required', not the closest-looking candidate. 'Comprise' already means 'consist of' or 'be made up of', so 'comprises of' is always wrong and must lose the 'of'.
rules.ok: The committee comprises nine members: this already needs no change.
rules.bad: Changing an already-correct 'comprises' because the option list offers a near-miss.

q-cf-fit.cue: A blank with two look-alike or sound-alike words among the four options.
q-cf-fit.standard: Decide what part of speech and what meaning the slot needs, then pick the member of the pair that has it.
q-cf-fit.fast: For noun-and-verb pairs, test whether 'a' or 'the' could stand in front of the blank: if it could, the noun is wanted.
q-cf-fit.eliminate: Cross out the unrelated options first; the real choice is almost always between two of the four.
traps: Advice and advise, practice and practise, effect and affect.
Principal and principle, stationary and stationery.
Eminent and imminent, continual and continuous, credible and credulous.

q-cf-spot.cue: A long sentence in which one word of a confused pair has been used for the other.
q-cf-spot.standard: Read each part and test any word you know to have a twin. Replace it with its partner and see which reading makes sense.
q-cf-spot.fast: Scan for the known pairs first: lie/lay, affect/effect, principal/principle.
q-cf-spot.eliminate: Parts with no word from a confused pair can be skipped.

q-cf-replace.cue: A full sentence with one phrase highlighted, and a fourth option 'No substitution required'.
q-cf-replace.standard: Decide what the highlighted phrase should say, then compare it letter by letter with the sentence's own wording before looking at the options.
q-cf-replace.fast: If the highlighted phrase is already exactly right, stop and pick 'No substitution required'; do not second-guess a correct phrase.
q-cf-replace.eliminate: Drop every option that merely adds a different wrong preposition or form; what remains is either the one correct phrase or 'No substitution required'.
traps: Assuming an error exists just because the question offers correction options.
'Comprises of' and 'is comprised of', both of which keep an unwanted 'of'.

pyqs.text:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.
During the briefing on the new city-bus timetable, the conductor explained that the route [[comprises of]] three major interchanges and two feeder loops, so commuters should keep extra time for transfers.
pyqs.why: 'Comprise' already means 'consist of' or 'be made up of', so it takes no 'of'; the highlighted 'comprises of' must become plain 'comprises'.

b.note: 'Is comprised of' turns 'comprise' passive and keeps an 'of' it does not need; the active 'comprises' is the correct fix.

c.note: 'Comprising of' keeps the same unwanted 'of' in a different grammatical form.

d.note: This says no change is needed, but 'comprises of' is a standard error; the 'of' must be dropped.

options: to lay down for an hour
practice.why: 'Lay' needs an object. To rest one's own body is 'to lie down', so it should be 'to lie down for an hour'.

a.note: 'After the long journey' is a correct phrase of time.

b.note: 'He went upstairs' is a correct main clause.

d.note: 'Before dinner' is a correct phrase of time.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

practice.why: 'Comprise' already means 'consist of', so it takes no 'of'; the highlighted phrase must lose the 'of' and become 'comprises'.

b.note: 'Is comprised of' is a common way to try to fix the error, but 'comprise' is active in sense and does not need the passive 'is ... of' either.

c.note: 'Comprising of' keeps the same unwanted 'of' in a different form.

d.note: This says no change is needed, but 'comprises of' is wrong; the 'of' must be dropped.

practice.text:

practice.why: The sentence already reads 'comprises' with no 'of', which is the correct form, so no substitution is required.

a.note: 'Comprises of' adds the unwanted 'of' that the sentence's own correct wording does not have.

b.note: 'Is comprised' drops the object entirely and reads as incomplete.

c.note: 'Comprise' (with no 's') does not agree with the singular subject 'the committee'.
